title: Find your way around the 3.7L accessory drive
introduction:
This is the belt-drive map for the 3.7L V6. The crankshaft turns the external pulleys and belts so the engine can power its accessories. The numbers identify components; they are not a removal sequence.

Start at **3, the crankshaft belt pulley**, then follow the blue belt paths in the original drawing. **2 is the accessory drive belt**, and **1 is its tensioner**, which keeps that belt under tension. The main path drives **6, the coolant pump pulley**, and **7, the generator pulley**. The pump circulates coolant; the generator supplies electrical power while the engine runs. Their pulleys are the drive wheels, not the complete pump or generator.

The drawing separately identifies **4, the A/C compressor belt**, and **5, the A/C compressor pulley**. Keeping those labels separate helps you choose the correct belt procedure and understand which part you are looking at. The A/C pulley transfers rotation to the compressor drive; the compressor itself works in the refrigerant circuit.

Use the numbered table to match each part to the drawing, then open its dedicated procedure for inspection or replacement. This map gives you orientation before the tools come out.

Continue with the [3.7L accessory drive belt procedure](#/document/G1688121) or the separate [3.7L A/C compressor belt procedure](#/document/G1688123) when you are ready for the actual work.
